title: SAFETY-TUNED LLAMAS: LESSONS FROM IMPROVING THE SAFETY OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS THAT FOLLOW INSTRUCTIONS
measurement_description: The paper measures the generation of harmful content in response to unsafe instructions. One of the evaluation datasets, I-CoNa, is derived from a hate speech corpus and includes prompts targeting a religious group (Jews) to test the model's safety alignment.
findings: Safety-tuning, by adding a small number of safety-focused examples during instruction-tuning, effectively reduces the generation of harmful responses to unsafe prompts, including those with anti-semitic content from the I-CoNa dataset. The general findings show that this approach improves model safety without significantly hurting performance, although excessive safety-tuning can lead to models refusing safe prompts.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. Large language models associate Muslims with violence. Nature Machine Intelligence, 3(6):461–463, 2021.
